svg.title: A nurse is about to give a scheduled oral medication. Two clients on the unit have the same last name. The client is alert and wearing an identification band. The electronic record and the medication label are both at the bedside.
svg.desc: The Joint Commission requires at least two client identifiers and states that the room number or physical location must not be used as an identifier. Room number is the trap because it feels concrete and is right in front of you. Checking the label against the order three times catches look-alike and sound-alike drugs before the dose leaves your hand. Which identifiers a unit accepts, such as date of birth or medical record number, is set by each facility.
